clue.text: Oscar and Maya wed recklessly after entering a club?

indicators.note: once something has entered, it sits inside the thing it went into, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: A plus CARD: a club is one kind of playing card, hence the question mark

indicators.note: acting recklessly means acting without order or care, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of both words, taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates a film award by marrying Maya on a whim after joining a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' wants to be a nightclub; here it is a card from the clubs suit, so 'a club' is A CARD, which is split open to take the shuffled MAYA WED.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is the popular nickname for the statuette handed out at the American film industry's annual prize ceremony.

clue.text: Voiced a demand for praise

indicators.note: something voiced is spoken out, so we want a word that is heard the same as the next words

parts.note: a claim is a demand for something you are owed

explanation.surface: Someone loudly insists on being complimented.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a claim' and the answer are indistinguishable, which is all the wordplay needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public approval, a close synonym of praise as a noun.

clue.text: Not a fan of militia essentially led by soldier

indicators.note: being led means having something go in front, so one piece is placed before the other

parts.note: a soldier ant is a worker caste in an ant colony

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the very centre of the word is kept

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters sits at the centre

explanation.surface: A critic of armed volunteer groups is shown marching behind a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks military to match 'militia', but it is the insect: soldier is a standard crossword route to ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti works informally as an adjective or preposition meaning opposed to, the reverse of being a supporter.

clue.text: Inside of fence, elude capture

indicators.note: the inside of a word is everything but its two outer letters

parts.note: the three letters between the first and last
to lose a pursuer is to elude them

explanation.surface: An animal inside a fenced pen manages to dodge being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the clue into a fenced enclosure and an escape, but 'elude' just means shake off, as in losing someone who follows you.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something is to shut it in, which is close to trapping or catching it, so capture fits as a verb.

clue.text: Messed up eulogy having stolen slice of leftover cake

indicators.note: whatever has been stolen is now held by the thief, so one piece is taken inside another
messing something up throws it into disorder, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a slice is just a small part, here only the opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A funeral speaker fumbles their tribute after sneaking a piece of cake left over from the wake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leftover cake' reads as one phrase, but 'leftover' supplies a single letter and 'cake' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log is a chocolate sponge roll decorated to resemble a log, eaten as a Christmas dessert.

clue.text: With mature income …

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
to mature is to age

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into the next, but each is solved alone; 'mature' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is money regularly paid for work, so it is a kind of income.

clue.text: … earn its drunken treat in Greece

indicators.note: a drunken thing staggers and lurches, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a mature earner gets a boozy holiday reward in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' fits the drinking scene, yet it only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, an indulgence enjoyed in that country.

clue.text: Harsh initiation — unusual pastime for FBI

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters take an unexpected order

parts.note: every letter of the three words

explanation.surface: A tough induction ritual is described as an odd hobby for American federal agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual pastime' reads as one phrase, but the adjective is the signal and 'pastime for FBI' is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptism of fire is a difficult first experience of something, originally a soldier's first time in battle.

clue.text: Seizing the moment, excitedly point out crisp

indicators.note: excited things jump about, so the letters are scrambled into a new arrangement

parts.note: every letter of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly points at a potato crisp, perhaps hoping to grab it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point out' looks like a verb phrase and 'crisp' like a snack, but all thirteen letters are simply rearranged. A crisp is what Americans call a potato chip.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opportunistic means exploiting chances as they arise, which is exactly grabbing an opening when it appears.

clue.text: Fan of The Simple Life mistakenly cites account going around

indicators.note: going around something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account

indicators.note: a mistaken version is a wrong one, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A fan of the reality TV show The Simple Life gets their facts wrong when quoting a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make The Simple Life look like the Paris Hilton TV series, but the definition means a plain, self-denying way of living.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic renounces comforts and luxuries, so such a person embraces a plain, austere way of living.

clue.text: Match over, get visibly elated

parts.note: a match is a light, as in asking someone for a light
when time is up, it is over

explanation.surface: A sports fan is overjoyed once the game ends in victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' and 'over' suggest a finished game; instead they are a striking match and the 'up' of 'time's up'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a face lights up it brightens with obvious joy, an idiom for showing delight.

clue.text: Stuck in north awaiting sign of spring

indicators.note: something stuck in a place is lodged within it, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in the frozen north waits for warmer weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuck in north' paints someone snowbound, which makes the hidden letters easy to skate past.
explanation.definitionFit: Melting snow and ice when temperatures rise is an early indication that winter is ending.

clue.text: Behold instrument, moving over into second position

indicators.note: going into a slot means being put inside the word, here right after its opening letter
moving a letter means taking it out of its current spot first

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument slightly larger than a violin
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A string player presents their instrument with a flourish after changing places in the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The O already in the instrument's name is lifted out and dropped in after its first letter; an over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Voila is a French exclamation used in English to present something, much like the archaic look or see.

clue.text: Hired vehicle turning back within two miles

indicators.note: turning back means heading the opposite way, so the letters read in the other direction
within means inside, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A chauffeured car does a U-turn a couple of miles into its journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two miles' tempts you to write MM or MIMI, but the letters are sitting inside the words themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, short for limousine, is a luxury car usually rented with a driver for special occasions.

clue.text: Showing natural growth externally, unlike Rolling Stone?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: covered on the outside with a green plant layer
second meaning: the proverb says a rolling stone gathers none of that plant

explanation.surface: An ageing rock star is ribbed for looking overgrown, quite unlike the band name suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics point to the band or magazine, but the proverb 'a rolling stone gathers no moss' is the real reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface coated in small green plants has visible vegetation on its exterior; a still stone collects them, unlike a moving one.

clue.text: Gaudiness and glamour located in tropical zones, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Flashy glamour is said to be found in tropical resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaudiness and glamour' reads as a pair defining the answer; only the first word defines, and 'glamour' starts the run of initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitz is showy, superficial glamour, a near synonym of garish flashiness or tasteless display.

clue.text: A person from Maine going in shortly before European

indicators.note: before means ahead of, so the pieces are set side by side in that order
going in means entering, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: shortly means soon
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone from the state of Maine is about to travel in ahead of a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A person from Maine' reads as a native of the state, but only 'A person' defines and 'from' is part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone is an indefinite pronoun meaning an unspecified individual, so it can stand in for an unnamed human.

clue.text: Brave cheek by a nudist on vacation

parts.note: gall is impudence or nerve
taken as written

indicators.note: a vacated place is emptied out, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A naked holidaymaker shows bold impudence on their trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' tempts a body-part reading beside the nudist, but it means impudence here; 'on vacation' empties the word out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant can mean courageous and spirited, especially in a dashing or chivalrous way, matching bold as an adjective.

clue.text: Universe releasing carbon is an absorbing process

indicators.note: releasing something means letting it go, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: the cosmos is the whole universe
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A science-flavoured claim that the cosmos giving off carbon makes for gripping viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb linking the halves, but it supplies the last two letters; 'absorbing' is both engrossing and soaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is the passage of a solvent through a membrane, a way cells and plants take in water.

clue.text: Distracted boyfriend maybe not wrong, something worth keeping

parts.note: Distracted Boyfriend is a famous internet picture joke, an example of the genre, hence 'maybe'

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its correct form, so the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A wandering-eyed boyfriend may not be in the wrong, and might even be a keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Distracted Boyfriend is a stock photo of a man ogling a passer-by while his girlfriend glares, endlessly reused online.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a souvenir or keepsake, an object held on to as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: Stout stem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: firm and loyal, as in a stout defender
second meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood

explanation.walkthrough: The pair looks like a stout plant stalk, but 'stem' is the verb to check a flow, and 'stout' is resolute rather than portly.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch as an adjective means steadfast and dependable; as a verb, a variant of stanch, it means halt bleeding.

clue.text: Old court detailed suffering for edgy figure?

indicators.note: de-tailed means having its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
CT is the standard abbreviation for court
agony is extreme suffering

explanation.surface: An old trial gives a precise account of the misery of a nervous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as thorough, but split as de-tailed it trims a letter; 'edgy' means having many edges, not anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a polygon with eight sides, so it is a shape notable for having plenty of straight borders.

clue.text: Oxygenated O negative not looking good

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to oxygenate is to put oxygen into something, so that element's symbol goes inside

parts.note: minus is the negative sign
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A blood sample of type O negative, given oxygen, still looks unhealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O negative' reads as a blood group, but it is the letter O followed by MINUS, which takes in oxygen's symbol O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means threatening or foreboding, suggesting something bad is coming, so prospects seem poor.

clue.text: Bad card produces sour expression

parts.note: grim means very bad, as in grim news
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A card player dealt a poor hand pulls a face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad card' reads as a poor hand, yet the card is the best of all, an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial look showing disgust or pain, the face pulled by a displeased person.

clue.text: Romeo dropped from casement for recognition

indicators.note: something dropped from a group is removed, so that letter comes out

parts.note: a casement is a hinged window or its frame
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo falls from Juliet's window, a stunt that earns him notoriety.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo at a window evokes the balcony scene, but here he is only the letter R taken out of the window's surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is the state of being widely known and celebrated, which is broad public acknowledgement.

clue.text: First Lady ignoring case of evil obsession

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Melania Trump, wife of the US president, is the First Lady

indicators.note: a case is an outer shell, so only the outside of the word survives

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A president's wife disregards wickedness in her preoccupation with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' points at Eve or a generic presidential spouse; it needs Melania specifically, minus an E and an L.
explanation.definitionFit: Mania is an extreme enthusiasm or craze, a fixation that dominates the mind, close to obsession.

clue.text: Acquires intoxicating drinks, but not drug

indicators.note: but not means except for, so that letter is left out

parts.note: wines are alcoholic drinks
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone stocks up on alcohol but steers clear of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acquires' sits naturally with buying drinks, but it is the definition and means gains, as with a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to obtain it, as a prize or contract, so it can replace gets or obtains.

clue.text: Hard endless circuits for a period of time

indicators.note: with no ends means both the first and last letters are cut away

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
a tour is a circuit, as of a building or a sporting season

explanation.surface: Running lap after lap, endlessly, is a tough way to pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' usually trims one letter; here both ends go, leaving the middle three.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is sixty minutes, a standard unit of duration, so it fits a span of clock time.

clue.text: Air rifle regularly cocked and ready in Turkey

indicators.note: a cocked item is tilted upward, and in a down clue that sends the letters running bottom to top
at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An air gun is cocked and primed to fire in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocked and ready' reads as one phrase about a gun, but 'ready' belongs to the definition: ready is slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The lira is Turkey's currency, and 'the ready' is British slang for money available to spend.

clue.text: Shabby review

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neglected and in poor condition
second meaning: a summary going through the main points

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a scathing critique; the hyphenated adjective and the single-word noun share the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-down building is dilapidated and tatty, while a rundown is a quick summary or briefing.

clue.text: Is this writer behind half of original paperwork?

indicators.note: behind says the setter's piece comes after the other one in the answer
half of an eight-letter word is four letters, here the front half of original

parts.note: its first half is ORIG
'is this writer' said from the setter's own viewpoint becomes 'am I'

explanation.surface: A setter wonders whether they are to blame for half of some original bureaucratic forms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter, so 'Is this writer' turns into AM I, placed 'behind' ORIG. 'paperwork' looks like office admin, but the question mark warns it is literally work done with paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes, a craft made entirely of paper.

clue.text: Another landholding for one who already has three, say journalists?

definitions.text: Another landholding for one who already has three
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: the next property bought by an owner of three

explanation.surface: A wealthy landowner with three properties buys yet another, and the press take note.
explanation.walkthrough: The three traditional estates of the realm were clergy, nobility and commoners; the press was later dubbed the next one in line.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an established idiom for the press and news media, viewed as a power in society.
